catalysts.headline: Agreed to sell a rare pediatric disease Priority Review Voucher (PRV) for $210 million.

Agreed to sell a second Priority Review Voucher for $210 million (announcement, not yet closed as of this report), this one tied to the Genglycos (DTX401) approval for glycogen storage disease type Ia; buyer undisclosed, sale subject to Hart-Scott-Rodino and other customary closing conditions. Combined with the Oct 14 FAYUVI-linked PRV sale, the two deals total roughly $413M.
catalysts.impact: Non-dilutive cash inflow of $210M upon closing

catalysts.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald raised price target to $39 (from $33), Overweight, raising probability-of-success on FAYUVI to 100% from 90%

FDA granted standard full approval to FAYUVI (UX111) for pediatric MPS IIIA (Sanfilippo syndrome Type A) — the first-ever FDA-approved treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome Type A and Ultragenyx's second gene therapy approval. (One source lists the decision date as 09/19/2026 instead — see conflicts.)

catalysts.headline: FDA granted full approval of FAYUVI (UX111, rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf) gene therapy, the first-ever approved treatment for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A (MPS IIIA); Ultragenyx received a Priority Review Voucher
catalysts.impact: shares jumped ~12.6-13%, with further gains after-hours

catalysts.headline: Ultragenyx's Phase 3 ASPIRE study of apazunersen (GTX-102) in Angelman syndrome missed its primary endpoint (change from baseline in Bayley-4 cognitive raw score) and its key secondary endpoint (Multidomain Responder Index net response); safety was consistent with the earlier Phase 1/2 data. Company said it is evaluating the program's disposition and will implement 'significant' expense reductions.
catalysts.impact: Shares fell approximately 44-46% (reported variously, e.g. close of $14.84 vs prior close, down $11.68/-44%); JPMorgan downgraded to Neutral from Overweight and cut its price target to $36 from $80; Evercore cut its target to $16; this appears NOT to be reflected in the on-file market cap/EPS figures, which are dated Aug 20, 2026 (pre-crash) — see conflicts

catalysts.headline: FDA approved GENGLYCOS gene therapy (Ultragenyx's other 2026 approval), which also came with a Priority Review Voucher
Q2 2026 results: record quarterly revenue $214M; net loss $92M / $0.90 per share; FY2026 revenue guidance $730M-$760M

conflicts: On-file market cap ($2.6B, as of 2026-08-20) predates the Sept 2, 2026 ~44-46% single-day drop following the failed Phase 3 ASPIRE (apazunersen/GTX-102) readout — resolved this pass with a newer, consistent reading ($1.54B as of 2026-10-26).

notes: Two Priority Review Voucher sales in October (10/7 for $210M, 10/14 for $203M tied to the FAYUVI approval) total $413M in non-dilutive cash — a significant update not previously on file. FAYUVI (UX111) received full FDA approval for pediatric MPS IIIA in 'September' 2026 per secondary sources, but no exact date was found, so it is NOT included as a dated catalyst — flagged here as important context only.
